messages:
prateek: Heads-up — I think we need a small follow-up RFC for how far the API contract should extend when a runtime is deployed in private mode and the control plane is degraded/unreachable. My proposal: define a tiny, explicit "local-proxy" capability that a private runtime can opt into. It should be purely a serving shim, not a control-plane takeover. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

samira: +1 on an explicit capability manifest. Avoid implicit feature expansion. If the runtime advertises a manifest we can treat it as a contract the control plane honors offline. Also we need clear defaults for telemetry and audit-forwarding.

alex: Sketch of a minimal manifest we can push in the bootstrap phase (private runtime writes, control plane validates when reachable):

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "local_proxy": true,
    "streaming": false,
    "kms_passthrough": "required"
  },
  "model_pin": "gpt-lite-v1",
  "max_batch_ms": 40
}
```

This stays intentionally small so we don't leak hosted-only semantics into private.

dina: Important: if we allow kms_passthrough, we must document the exact key-wrapping flow and what the control plane sees. Also add a telemetry flag like `audit_forwarding: best_effort` so customers know we can drop logs if network fails.

infra-bot: DeployBot: private-runtime/rt-42 reported control-plane-heartbeat-miss at 4755551270 — local-proxy active.

marie: For fallback semantics, recommend a deterministic circuit-breaker: if control-plane unreachable for >2m, runtime flips to "offline-serving" mode and uses the manifest. If an incoming request needs an unsupported op (eg function-calling when streaming=false) respond with a clear 4xx and an actionable body that SDKs can surface. Example approach: return 422 + machine-parsable reason + `fallback_route` hint.

prateek: Agree. Minimal API change: add header `X-Redwood-Env: private-local` and a well-known error shape for unsupported ops. We should also add a small SDK mapping so clients can surface fallback behavior instead of crashing.

alex: Example HTTP response we can standardize on for unsupported ops in offline-serving:

`HTTP/1.1 422 Unsupported-Operation`

Body: `{"error":"unsupported_operation","reason":"streaming_not_available","fallback":"hosted:gpt-lite-v1"}`

samira: Rollout plan: canary this for a few enterprise customers on Dedicated first (they already have HA + SLAs) and add an e2e test harness simulating control-plane failure so we can catch bad semantics before wider Private rollout.

dina: Add runbook snippet for ops: how to flip the circuit breaker back when control-plane recovers, and what logs to expect so support can tell if the runtime was serving from manifest.

prateek: Action items: 1) I will draft the short RFC with manifest shape + error contract + runbook. 2) @alex will add SDK mapping PR for 422 fallback. 3) @samira will own canary list + test harness scenarios. I'll ping when draft is ready.

marie: +1 — also add a short privacy note about telemetry redaction when `audit_forwarding` is `best_effort` so legal can sign off.

samira: acked.

prateek: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC link here when it's up. :slightly_smiling_face:
